audit.why: Poppy 52.34% over 726 games; TRICKY 7.5/10 is fair. Sett owns levels 1-5 through Grit, Poppy reclaims the lane once her kit goes gold-independent.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: the chart handed Sett 5 of 7 stages while Poppy wins 52.34%. Two rows also contradicted their own text — win[4] said Sett while whys[4] says 'Genuinely even at 6', and win[6] said Skill while whys[6] and spikes[3] both say Poppy reclaims it at two items.
audit.why: Level 6 is the ult-trade row and the text already calls it even; two items is where Q's max-HP chunk and the wall stun outlast his flat base damage.
audit.corrected: Row 4 to Skill, row 6 to Poppy, in both layers as one group, with ratings brought in line. Rows 3 and 5 left on Skill so the chart no longer reads as a losing lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two kit errors. (1) 'W any dash he tries — his mobility is a suggestion': Sett has no dash — Knuckle Down is a move-speed steroid toward champions, Haymaker and Facebreaker are stationary. (2) Facebreaker was called a grab-stun; it only stuns when it catches enemies on opposite sides of him, otherwise it slows.
audit.why: Steadfast Presence has nothing to eat in this lane, so telling the user to hold W for a dash wastes the ability. And in a 1v1 Facebreaker is a slow unless Sett lines the user up with a minion on his far side — that changes every all-in.
audit.corrected: W restated as the armor/MR steroid, Facebreaker's both-sides condition stated, and Haymaker's shield named (the missing-interaction flag): it absorbs your burst window, so force it out before committing. Keeper's Verdict's untargetability during the charge is the answer to The Show Stopper.

audit.whatIsWrong: Haymaker was tracked as a cooldown only; its Grit bar matters more than its 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s timer.
audit.why: A full Grit bar is what makes the trade lethal, and Grit is fed by the damage you deal him.
audit.corrected: Advice re-pointed at the Grit bar plus the real cooldown.

audit.why: The common-mistakes list (feed grit, eat W true damage, get E-stunned) is accurate and not split by elo.

edits.before: His E grab-stun into double-punch and W smash bursts you harder than your flat 3-point combo.

edits.before: Sett's level 2-3 grit trades hurt — his W stores your damage and smashes it back as true damage, so don't extend on his W cooldown.
edits.after: Sett's level 2-3 Grit trades hurt — Haymaker turns your damage into a shield plus a true-damage smash, so never commit into a full Grit bar.

edits.before: Both ult: his R suppress-slam vs your Keeper's Verdict — you can knock him out of his all-in or W-block nothing since his R is a suppress, so save W for his E grab.
edits.after: Both ult at 6: The Show Stopper carries and slams and W cannot stop it — but Keeper's Verdict makes you untargetable through the charge, so it drops his grab entirely.

edits.before: Sett owns these levels — his W stores the damage you deal him and smashes it back as true damage, so every extended trade feeds his grit. Don't sit in his face throwing Q; his double-punch passive and E grab-stun out-trade your flat low base damage at 2-3. Use your W's passive armor/MR to soften his hits and only commit E when there's a wall to stun him against — a naked E just shoves him and tickles. Last-hit with Q's max-HP chunk and respect his W cooldown.
edits.after: Sett owns these levels — Haymaker stores the damage you deal him and returns it as a shield plus true damage, so every extended trade feeds his Grit. Don't sit in his face throwing Q. One thing in your favour: Facebreaker stuns only when it catches enemies on both sides of him, so alone in lane it is a slow unless he lines you up with a minion. Use W's passive armor/MR to soften his punches and commit E only with a wall behind him — a naked E just shoves him.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 still belong to Sett — his grit trades scale harder than your point-stagnant flat damage. At 6 it evens out: his R is a suppress-slam, not a dash, so your W won't block it, but your Keeper's Verdict can interrupt or displace his all-in. Save W to ground nothing here — hold it instead for peel, and bait his E grab before you commit. Don't trade into a full W charge; let it expire, then Q-chunk and reset.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 still belong to Sett — his Grit trades scale harder than your point-stagnant flat damage. At 6 it evens out: The Show Stopper carries and slams, so W won't stop it, but Keeper's Verdict makes you untargetable mid-charge and drops the grab. Bait Facebreaker, his only lockdown, before you commit. Never trade into a full Grit bar; let Haymaker expire, then Q-chunk and reset.

edits.before: Land E grab into his double-punch passive and W smash for a chunky level-2-3 burst
edits.after: Line you up with a minion so Facebreaker stuns, then punch into a Haymaker smash

notes: Packet defect 'never names any of Sett's abilities' is now partly addressed — Haymaker, Facebreaker, Knuckle Down and The Show Stopper all appear by name. Facebreaker's opposite-sides stun condition was absent from the page entirely and is the single most useful missing fact in this lane. Level chart rows 4 and 6 were contradicting their own whys text; fixed as a pair per layer. Rows 3 and 5 deliberately left on Skill rather than following the packet to Sett, since the packet itself flags the Sett-heavy chart as contradicting a 52.34% win rate.
